q: Atalanta play their home matches in which northern Italian city?
hint: Atalanta are Bergamo's club through and through: the stadium sits in the Borgo Santa Caterina district and the famous academy is at Zingonia, just outside the city.

q: In which year was Atalanta founded?
hint: The club was formed on 17 October 1907 by students of Bergamo's Liceo Classico Paolo Sarpi; a 1920 merger with fellow Bergamo side Bergamasca added the 'Bergamasca' to the name that survives today as Atalanta Bergamasca Calcio.

q: Atalanta sold their reigning Serie A top scorer to Juventus in 1997. Which striker had they sold to Juventus the previous summer, after one season in Bergamo?
hint: Vieri joined Atalanta from Venezia in 1995, moved to Juventus in July 1996 and won the Scudetto there before leaving for Atletico Madrid.

q: Who scored twice as Atalanta won 3-0 away to Liverpool in the 2024 Europa League quarter-final first leg?
hint: Scamacca struck just before half-time and again on the hour at Anfield, and Pašalić added a late third; Liverpool won the return leg 1-0 but went out 3-1 on aggregate.

q: Which winger came through Atalanta's youth system and was sold to Juventus in January 2020 for €35m while on loan at Parma?
hint: Sweden-raised Kulusevski was developed by Atalanta, broke through on loan at Parma, and was sold to Juventus mid-season while staying at Parma until June.

q: Which winger came through Atalanta's youth system in his native Bergamo province and joined Milan in 1986, going on to win the European Cup there?
hint: Born in Cisano Bergamasco, Donadoni debuted for Atalanta in 1982 and made 96 league appearances before Milan signed him — a year before Arrigo Sacchi arrived to build his great side.

q: Which nickname, taken from their striped shirts, do Atalanta share with Inter?
hint: Nerazzurri simply means 'the black-and-blues'. Atalanta are also called the Orobici, after the ancient Orobii people of the Bergamo hills.

q: Atalanta's nickname 'La Dea' translates into English as what?
hint: The club takes its name from Atalanta, the fleet-footed huntress of Greek myth, whose profile appears on the crest — Bergamo fans give her a rank above mortal.

q: Atalanta won their first major trophy by beating which club 3-1 in the 1963 Coppa Italia final?
hint: Angelo Domenghini scored a hat-trick at San Siro. The celebrations were muted — Bergamo-born Pope John XXIII died the following day.

q: Atalanta sold which midfielder to Juventus in August 2024?
hint: Koopmeiners had arrived from AZ in 2021 and left for a guaranteed fee of around €51m plus bonuses — one of the biggest sales in Atalanta's history.

q: Atalanta scored 98 Serie A goals in 2019-20 without a single player reaching 20 in the league. Which two shared the club's league top-scorer spot on 18 each?
hint: Muriel matched Zapata's 18 despite starting only 10 league games; with Iličić also on 15, Atalanta were the first Italian side since Juventus in 1951-52 to have three players score 15 or more.

q: Gian Piero Gasperini was appointed Atalanta coach in June 2016. Which club had he spent the previous three seasons managing?
hint: Gasperini left Genoa, where he was in his second spell from 2013 to 2016, to take charge of an Atalanta side that had just finished 13th.

q: In February 2022 the Percassi family sold a large stake in Atalanta to a group led by which American investor?
hint: Pagliuca, a Bain Capital co-chairman and Boston Celtics co-owner, led the group that took 55%; the Percassi family kept 45% and stayed the largest single shareholder, with Pagliuca named co-chairman.

q: Josip Iličić scored four goals in a single Champions League knockout match for Atalanta in March 2020. Who were the opponents?
hint: Atalanta won 4-3 at an empty Mestalla for an 8-4 aggregate victory; Iličić became the first player to score four in an away Champions League knockout tie.

q: Atalanta lost their opening three group games in the 2019-20 Champions League and still reached the last 16. Which club did they beat 3-0 away in the final group match to go through?
hint: After defeats to Dinamo Zagreb, Shakhtar and Manchester City, Atalanta took seven points from the last three games and won in Kharkiv to finish second.

q: Which Argentina international captained Atalanta before a bust-up with Gasperini led to his move to Sevilla in January 2021?
hint: The row reportedly began at half-time of a Champions League tie with Midtjylland on 1 December 2020, when he refused to switch to the right flank. Sevilla paid around €5m plus add-ons weeks later.

q: Which former Atalanta player turned retail entrepreneur was club president from 1990 to 1994 and returned in 2010 to launch its modern era?
hint: Percassi bought the club back in June 2010, weeks after relegation to Serie B, and rebuilt it around the Zingonia academy and a self-sustaining transfer model.

q: Who captained Atalanta to the 2010-11 Serie B title, only to be banned from football months later for match-fixing?
hint: Doni scored 12 goals from midfield as Atalanta went straight back up as champions, then received a three-and-a-half-year ban in August 2011 in the Scommessopoli betting scandal.

q: Atalanta qualified for the Champions League for the first time by finishing third in which Serie A season?
hint: A final-day comeback win over Sassuolo in May 2019 sealed third place on 69 points, edging out Inter and Milan.

q: Atalanta's 1987-88 Cup Winners' Cup run began with a shock 2-1 defeat away to which Welsh club, then playing in English non-league football?
hint: Merthyr, Welsh Cup holders, won 2-1 at Penydarren Park in September 1987; Atalanta needed a 2-0 win in Bergamo to scrape through 3-2 on aggregate and then went all the way to the semi-finals.

q: Atalanta sold which striker to Manchester United in the summer of 2023?
hint: Højlund had joined from Sturm Graz a year earlier and left for a fee reported at around £72m after a single Serie A season.

q: In 1987-88 Atalanta reached the Cup Winners' Cup semi-finals while playing in Serie B. Which Belgian club knocked them out and went on to win the trophy?
hint: Mechelen won both legs 2-1 and then beat Ajax in the final. Atalanta were in the competition as Coppa Italia runners-up, because winners Napoli had done the double and entered the European Cup.

q: Which coach guided Atalanta to the Serie B title in both 2005-06 and 2010-11?
hint: Colantuono had more than one spell in Bergamo and won promotion as champions in each of those seasons — the second time at the first attempt after relegation.

q: Where did Atalanta play their home Champions League matches during their debut 2019-20 campaign?
hint: Their Bergamo ground was in the middle of a major redevelopment, so Atalanta asked Inter and Milan for the use of San Siro. The work was finished in time for them to host European nights in Bergamo from 2020-21.

q: Atalanta's ground, opened in 1928 and long known as the Stadio Atleti Azzurri d'Italia, took the name of which sponsor in 2019?
hint: Gewiss, an electrical components firm from the Bergamo area, agreed the naming-rights deal that took effect on 1 July 2019, as the club began rebuilding the old ground stand by stand; the Gewiss Stadium name ran until 2025.

q: Who scored a hat-trick as Atalanta beat Bayer Leverkusen 3-0 to win the 2024 Europa League final?
hint: Lookman's three goals in Dublin ended Leverkusen's unbeaten season and gave Atalanta only their second major trophy, more than 60 years after the first.

q: Atalanta led 1-0 in the 2020 Champions League quarter-final before conceding twice in the closing minutes. Which club knocked them out?
hint: Mario Pašalić had put Atalanta ahead in Lisbon before Marquinhos and Eric Choupo-Moting struck at the death for PSG.

q: Which striker finished as Serie A's top scorer in 1996-97 with 24 goals, in what proved to be his only season at Atalanta?
hint: Inzaghi arrived from Parma and won the Capocannoniere in his single Bergamo campaign, edging Vincenzo Montella, before Juventus signed him that summer.

q: As of 2026, Atalanta's most recent relegation from Serie A came at the end of which season?
hint: Atalanta finished 18th in 2009-10 and went down, but won Serie B at the first attempt and have been a top-flight club ever since — the end of decades of yo-yoing.

q: Which Atalanta forward's 25 goals made him Serie A's top scorer in 2024-25?
hint: Retegui arrived in 2024 and finished six clear of Moise Kean, becoming only the second Atalanta player to win the capocannoniere.

q: Atalanta's fiercest rivalry, the Derby Lombardo, is contested with which neighbouring club?
hint: Bergamo and Brescia sit around 50km apart and their mutual dislike long predates football — a textbook case of Italian campanilismo that has produced some of Serie A's most volatile scenes.

q: Claudio Caniggia was an Atalanta player when he scored the goal that knocked Brazil out of the 1990 World Cup. Which Serie A club had Atalanta signed him from the year before?
hint: Caniggia left River Plate for Verona in 1988 and moved to Bergamo in 1989, scoring 26 goals in 85 league games across three years at Atalanta.

q: After leaving Atalanta in 2025, Gian Piero Gasperini took over at which Serie A club?
hint: He replaced the retiring Claudio Ranieri in the Roma dugout, while Ivan Jurić was appointed in Bergamo.
